collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager wonders whether to tell a neighbor their roof is sagging: the friend says yes, or says leave it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has noticed that (subject.his/her) neighbor's roof is sagging badly on one side. The neighbor doesn't seem to have noticed, or doesn't care. (subject) doesn't want to be rude. (subject.He/she) asks (friend) whether (friend.he/she) should say something.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I'd want to know," says (friend). So (subject) mentions it, carefully, to the neighbor. The neighbor looks at the roof, sighs and says, "I know. I just haven't had the time." (subject) offers to help on (subject.his/her) next free day. The neighbor accepts. The roof gets fixed. It wasn't a secret after all. It was just a chore.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "It's their roof," says (friend). "They'll fix it when they want to." (subject) leaves it. A month later the neighbor fixes it all by (subject.him/her)self. (subject) wonders if saying something would have been better or worse. (subject.He/she) decides it doesn't matter. The roof's fine.
